momo.name: Momo
momo.description: Steamed or fried bite-sized dumplings filled with minced meat (buff, chicken, pork) or finely shredded vegetables, seasoned with aromatic Himalayan spices.
momo.cultural_significance: Undoubtedly Nepal's unofficial national comfort dish and most popular culinary export, cherished across generations and gatherings.
momo.recipe_summary: Roll thin dough circles, fill with spiced stuffing, pleat into crescent or pouch shapes, and steam in a layered steamer for 10-12 minutes.
momo.suggested_accompaniments: Served piping hot with fiery tomato-sesame achar and roasted timur (Sichuan pepper) dip.

selroti.name: Selroti
selroti.description: Ring-shaped traditional Nepali sweet fried rice bread with a crispy exterior and soft, airy crumb.
selroti.cultural_significance: Indispensable symbol of festive celebrations including Dashain, Tihar, wedding rituals, and ceremonial pujas.
selroti.recipe_summary: Semi-liquid rice batter is beaten until fluffy, then hand-poured in circular rings into smoking-hot ghee or oil and flipped with wooden sticks until golden brown.
selroti.suggested_accompaniments: Freshly brewed masala milk tea (Chiya), spicy aloo achar, or sukuti.

dalbhat.name: Dal Bhat Tarkari
dalbhat.description: The quintessence of daily Nepali life: steamed white or brown rice (Bhat) served alongside slow-cooked lentil soup (Dal) and seasonal spiced vegetables (Tarkari).
dalbhat.cultural_significance: Consumed twice daily by millions, captured by the beloved mountaineering phrase 'Dal Bhat Power 24 Hour'.
dalbhat.recipe_summary: Lentils are boiled and tempered (chhonk) with ghee, garlic, and jimbu. Accompanied by pan-sautéed vegetable curry, fresh greens (Saag), and tomato chutney.
dalbhat.suggested_accompaniments: Fermented radish pickle (Mula ko Achar), fried sun-dried papad, and fresh sliced lemons.

dhido.name: Dhido
dhido.origin: Hilly and mountainous regions of Nepal
dhido.description: A dense, highly nutritious hot porridge-like mash prepared by continuously stirring buckwheat, millet (kodo), or corn flour in boiling water.
dhido.cultural_significance: A heritage food deeply rooted in rural agrarian life, praised for sustained stamina and clean energy.
dhido.recipe_summary: Water is brought to a boil in a thick iron cauldron (Tawo/Karahi), flour is gradually rained in while vigorously whipped with a wooden paddle (Dabiro) until glossy and pliable.
dhido.suggested_accompaniments: Eaten without chewing by dipping small morsels directly into Gundruk soup, rich local chicken gravy, or fresh curd.

gundruk.name: Gundruk
gundruk.description: Sun-dried fermented leafy green vegetables (mustard, radish, or cauliflower leaves) renowned for their appetizing tang and deep umami richness.
gundruk.cultural_significance: Considered the national vegetable dish of Nepal, reflecting ancestral wisdom in seasonal food preservation.
gundruk.recipe_summary: Leaves are wilted, packed into airtight clay pots for microbial fermentation, sun-dried, and subsequently cooked into a warm spiced soup with potatoes and soybeans (Bhatmas).
gundruk.suggested_accompaniments: Served as Gundruk Jhol with steaming Dhido or hot boiled rice.

yomari.name: Yomari
yomari.description: Fig-shaped steamed rice flour dumpling filled with sweet molten molasses (Chaku) and sesame seeds, or savory lentil paste.
yomari.cultural_significance: Centerpiece of Yomari Punhi, celebrating the post-harvest full moon and bestowing prosperity and blessings upon families.
yomari.recipe_summary: Warm dough is sculpted with fingers into pointed conical figures, hollowed out, packed with warm chaku-sesame filling, pinched closed, and steamed.
yomari.suggested_accompaniments: Eaten warm when the inner chaku is delightfully molten.

panipuri.name: Panipuri
panipuri.origin: Pan-South Asian street culture with iconic Nepali spicy-tangy twists
panipuri.description: Crisp, hollow fried semolina dough balls (puris) punctured and stuffed with mashed spiced potatoes, chickpeas, and plunged into ice-cold tart herbal mint-tamarind water.
panipuri.cultural_significance: Beloved social street ritual across Kathmandu, Pokhara, and town squares throughout Nepal.
panipuri.recipe_summary: Hollow sphere is lightly crushed on top, spooned with seasoned potato filling, immersed in zesty herbal water, and eaten whole in one bite.

sekuwa.name: Sekuwa
sekuwa.description: Tender chunks of meat marinated in pungent mustard oil, garlic, raw spices, and slow-roasted over fragrant natural wood charcoal coals.
sekuwa.cultural_significance: Quintessential Nepali barbecue, famous for lively evening gatherings and celebratory celebrations.
sekuwa.recipe_summary: Meat is rubbed thoroughly with aromatic spice paste, skewered on iron rods, and rotated over glowing charcoal until smoky and lightly charred.
sekuwa.suggested_accompaniments: Served with beaten rice (Baji/Chiura), pickled radishes, and toasted soybeans.

juju_dhau.name: Juju Dhau
juju_dhau.description: Rich, velvety sweet yogurt set in traditional porous unglazed terracotta clay pots, revered as the 'King of Curd'.
juju_dhau.cultural_significance: A heritage sweet crafted for centuries in historic Bhaktapur, consumed at celebrations, festivals, and sacred rites.
juju_dhau.recipe_summary: Buffalo milk is boiled and reduced until dense, naturally sweetened, seasoned with gentle aromatics, poured into breathable earthenware pots, and insulated in rice husks to set.
juju_dhau.suggested_accompaniments: Enjoyed chilled as a celebratory dessert or after a traditional Newari feast.

samosa.name: Samosa & Tarkari
samosa.origin: Terai & Pahad tea stalls across Nepal
samosa.description: Flaky, crisp pyramid pastries filled with tempered diced potatoes, green peas, and whole cumin, commonly served topped with savory chickpea curry (Tarkari).
samosa.cultural_significance: The most widely enjoyed morning and afternoon tea-time companion across roadside tea stalls in Nepal.
samosa.recipe_summary: Crisp flour pastry is folded into neat cones, stuffed with spiced potato mixture, sealed, and deep-fried at gentle temperatures until golden amber.
samosa.suggested_accompaniments: Hot chana tarkari (chickpea gravy) with sweet-tangy tamarind chutney.

kwati.name: Kwati
kwati.origin: Newar community and broad Nepali tradition
kwati.description: Hearty, nourishing thick stew brewed from nine distinct varieties of sprouted beans, simmered with warming spices, lovage seeds, and ginger.
kwati.cultural_significance: Sacred culinary tradition prepared during the festival of Janai Purnima (Gunhu Punhi) for inner strength and seasonal vitality.
key_ingredients: Nine sprouted beans (black gram, chickpea, field pea, soybean, mung, cowpea, kidney bean, faba bean, gram)
kwati.recipe_summary: Sprouted beans are tempered in mustard oil with aromatic jowano, sautéed with aromatics, and pressure cooked into a thick, aromatic therapeutic broth.
kwati.suggested_accompaniments: Paired with warm steamed rice or flaky flatbreads.

bara.name: Bara (Wo)
bara.dietary: Vegetarian (Can be topped with egg or minced meat)
bara.description: Nutritious golden lentil patties made from ground black gram or green mung bean paste, lightly pan-fried in mustard oil on a concave griddle.
bara.cultural_significance: Integral component of auspicious ritual feasts (Sagan) symbolizing goodwill, fortune, and celebration.
bara.recipe_summary: Soaked lentils are ground into a smooth thick paste, whipped until airy, spooned onto an oiled griddle, flattened into round discs, and shallow-fried till crispy on edges.
bara.suggested_accompaniments: Served with spicy potato gravy (Aloo ko Jhol) or freshly cracked egg topping.

chatpate.name: Chatpate
chatpate.description: Crisp, pungent, and explosive street snack tossed to order from puffed rice, dry Wai Wai instant noodles, boiled potatoes, chickpeas, raw onions, and freshly squeezed lemon juice.
chatpate.cultural_significance: Synonymous with school and college nostalgia, street corners, and lively gatherings.
chatpate.recipe_summary: All ingredients are rapidly hand-tossed inside a repurposed metal tin with a spoon and served in newspaper cones with bamboo picks.
chatpate.suggested_accompaniments: Enjoyed instantly on foot with friends!

chow_mein.name: Nepali Chow Mein
chow_mein.description: Wok-tossed egg or flour noodles stir-fried with julienned cabbage, carrots, bell peppers, sliced chicken or buff, dressed in a distinctive dark soy and cumin-coriander spice kick.
chow_mein.cultural_significance: The perennial cafeteria and roadside diner classic across every city and village throughout Nepal.
chow_mein.recipe_summary: A smoking hot wok is fired with oil, garlic, and sliced meat or vegetables, noodles are introduced, tossed vigorously with seasonings until fragrant and glazed.
chow_mein.suggested_accompaniments: Drizzled with house-made chili tomato ketchup and fresh pickled chillies.

thukpa.name: Thukpa
thukpa.origin: Himalayan communities / Sherpa & Tibetan culture in Nepal
thukpa.description: Steaming, restorative noodle soup packed with hand-pulled or long wheat noodles, vegetables, sliced meat, and a deeply aromatic spice-infused broth.
thukpa.cultural_significance: A beloved winter food providing warmth and restorative nourishment during cold Himalayan months.
thukpa.recipe_summary: A fragrant spiced soup stock is simmered with vegetables and protein, then poured piping hot over freshly blanched noodles in deep ceramic bowls.
thukpa.suggested_accompaniments: Served with spicy garlic-chili oil paste on the side.

chiya.name: Masala Chiya
chiya.description: Rich, aromatic spiced milk tea brewed with full-bodied local CTC tea leaves (Ilam), fresh milk, and fragrant whole spices.
chiya.cultural_significance: The heart of Nepali hospitality and social culture; no guest enters a home without being greeted with a steaming glass of Chiya.
chiya.recipe_summary: Water and milk are brought to a roll with crushed spices and ginger, black tea is added and slow-boiled until deep amber, strained into glasses.
chiya.suggested_accompaniments: Paired with morning Selroti, bakery biscuits, or Malpuwa.
